newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Prudential Australia new business up 42 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Prudential Australia new business up 42 pct.

text.p: Superannuation and investment management group Prdutential Corp Australia Ltd said on Thursday its new business rose 42 percent in calendar 1996 to A$1.1 billion.
This compared with A$779.1 million in 1995.

Prudential Australia, a wholly owned subsidiary of Prudential Corp Plc, said its regular premium contributions rose 21 percent to A$86.7 million, while single premium business rose 14 percent to A$760.2 million. The biggest margins of growth came from the group investment business, comprising segregated funds and unit trusts, which leapt 480 percent to A$262 million.

"The results are particularly encouraging for Prudential given that a considerable part of last year was spent repositioning the group as part of a company-wide strategic review," Prudential Australia's managing director Trevor Perry told a media briefing.
Perry said Prudential Australia's results for 1996 indicated the group was well-placed to strengthen its position in its core business of superannuation, investments and life insurance.
Perry said Prudential had undertaken a massive change program over the past 12 to 18 months designed to reposition the company for the longer term.

"We have centralised our client servicing operations to make a single point of contact for our customers. We have supported this move by introducing Image and Workflow technology to improve customer service," he said.
The group's earnings report for the year to December 31, 1996 is expected to released in March.
